newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs seen turning to profits this year.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs seen turning to profits this year.

text.p: After showing paper losses in 1996 Poland's National Investment Funds (NFIs) should swing to profits this year on improved operating results of their firms and sales of strategic stakes in some of them, analysts said.

Analysts said the majority of the 15 funds showed heavy losses last year following a rise in depreciation charges, the creation of risk provisions and sales of non-productive assets of companies often at below their book value.
But they said those book cleaning operations should be largely over by now.

They also said next year's removal of corporate income tax exemption on capital gains on sales of firms in the funds' portfolio could make them intensify spinning off some of their shareholdings this year to take advantage of the tax break.

"There is even a chance all funds will show profits in the first quarter and in 1997...especially if they want to intensify selling of their companies to avoid paying tax next year," said Jacek Koczwara, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.

Krzysztof Nowinski, financial director of NFI Hetman said the fund, which had a 92.9-million-zloty net loss in 1996, should show profit in 1997 due to expected firms' operating profits and a likely sale of five or six of its companies.
"Next year funds' earnings should depend on their companies' operating profits...we expect our net profit to amount to tens of millions zlotys," he said.
Analysts said, however, that by rushing some deals and selling firms before their restructuring is fully underway, the funds might fail to get the best possible prices.
They also said the looming tax might weaken the funds' negotiating position and make potential investors bid lower.

But some fund officials, who asked not to be named, said the introduction of the tax might did not have to bring about a dramatic change as its impact could be largely softened thanks to some financial engineering.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in more than 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
